_note: Motion tokens for the HUD and menus (plan-cinematic section 8, P12.6). Tools/web/motion-css.mjs writes Web/Client/css/motion.css from this file; Sim/Cine/Motion reads it for Unity. Key suffix sets the unit: Ms is milliseconds, Px is pixels, Items is a count, Curve is a cubic bezier [x1, y1, x2, y2]. CSS names are --motion- plus the key in kebab case without the suffix.

focusMs.why: The focus ring moves in 80 ms, quick enough that a stick or arrow press feels instant.

panelOpenMs.why: A panel slides and fades in over 160 ms, so the eye follows it without waiting on it.

panelCloseMs.why: Leaving is a little faster than arriving, so going back never feels slow.

largeMoveMs.why: Bigger moves, such as a whole screen sliding over, get a little longer so they stay easy to follow.

countUpMs.why: Money changes count up over 400 ms on Easy and Normal. Tycoon and reduced motion show the final number at once.

slidePx.why: A short 12 px slide shows where a panel came from without a long trip across the screen.

staggerMs.why: List items start 30 ms apart, so a list reads top to bottom as it arrives.

staggerMaxItems.why: Only the first 5 items stagger; the rest start with the fifth, so a long list never makes the player wait.

reduceFadeMs.why: With reduced motion every slide becomes a plain fade of 120 ms or less, with no stagger and no count up.

easeOutCurve.why: One ease out curve for things arriving: fast start, soft landing, no overshoot and no bounce.

easeInCurve.why: One ease in curve for things leaving: soft start, quick exit, no overshoot and no bounce.
